posts.topic_title: Please please help me find my processing error!
posts.author: Justin W
posts.post_subject: Please please help me find my processing error!
posts.content_md:
Howdy again fellas!

Well, things are going great - real laser, making bright H2's, etc....

EXCEPT

I keep getting weird red marks on the edge/edges of my developed and dried plates. I'm reasonably sure it's a developing error vs. exposure problem mainly because the markings have a liquidy look to them - in extreme cases, drop-like spatters...

The markings I speak of are quite visible on the left edge of the plate in this image: [http://www.geocities.com/nowyermessingw ... ram003.jpg](http://www.geocities.com/nowyermessingwithasonofabitch/Coralgram003.jpg)

I am shooting on VRP-M 2.5X2.5 I develop with JD-2 plus following measures:

My processing routine is as follows:

1 Finish exposure

2 Take plate by edges into kitchen, shielding from air with cupped hand

3 Lay plate emulsion up in JD-2 Part A&B

4 Begin tipping tray as I start 2 minute timer

5 Tip tray for 2 minutes

5 Timer beeps. I pull on glove, rinse fingertips with tapwater, shake excess water from glove

6 Grasp plate by opposite corners, remove from A&B, hold plate vertical just over tray and shake excess developer off

7 Place plate emulsion up in distilled water stop bath, tip tray for a minute or two

8 Rinse and remove glove

9 Remove plate by opposite corners, shake excess stop bath from plate

10 Place plate emulsion up in bleach, begin tipping tray immediately

11 Tip tray until plate is clear of any swirls

12 Pull glove back on, rinse fingertips under sink again for good measure, shake excess water from glove

13 Turn on kitchen lights

14 Find plate in bleach, grasp by opposite corners and hold vertically over tray, shake off excess bleach

15 Place plate emulsion up in distilled water bleach stop, begin tipping tray immediately, wash until plate is no longer orange

16 Rinse and remove glove

17 Go back to tipping bleach stop tray for a few minutes

18 Start cold (but not *that*cold, here in FL) tap water running into collander in sink

19 Tip bleach stop for another few moments

20 Grasp plate by opposite corners, remove, shake of excess

21 Place plate emulsion up in collander under running tap water

22 Stroll about my apartment to get the kinks out while my plate washes

23 Return to sink, grasp plate by opposite corners, wash underside and emulsion side again under running water, shake off excess, pray FL water ordinance guys don't come for me

24 Place plate emulsion up in wetting agent WITH ADDED TABLE SUGAR

25 Tip tray for 1 minute by stopwatch

26 Grasp plate by opposite corners, remove horizontally from wetting agent, rolling plate in circular motion so liquid sheets off in all directions

27 Lay flat emulsion up on paper towel

28 squeegy from corner-to-corner with short length of windshield wiper blade stiffened with spring steel inserts

29 Turn A/C back on

30 It's Miller Time

Weird red blobby stuff along the edges of some of my plates... 

Any clue why? 

Please?

posts.topic_title: Please please help me find my processing error!
posts.author: Tom B.
posts.post_subject: Please please help me find my processing error!
posts.content_md:
From the example you posted it's hard to tell if it's a squeegee problem or not... You usually see streaks where the squeegee slipped and large blobs at the edge where it missed entirely, but drops are unusual. When squeegeeing I can usually spot any streaks and missed spots by inspecting the reflections from a safelight about 4-6 feet away and give the plate another swipe if needed before drying . You could experiment by repeatedly soaking and squeegeeing a dud plate under various lighting conditions and then under the safelight to see what to look for. I think a fairly distant light source is best to show up the wet spots.

Another cause would be that the gelatin has hardened unevenly in some areas so the swelling is uneven. I had had edge defects that look similar to this with plates from various manufacturers, but fortunately they have been infrequent. If you are confident that your soaking and squeegeeing technique is OK, then it's likely a plate defect. Plan your compositions to allow generous edge cropping

posts.content_md: Sorry, somehow managed to miss the fact that you were shooting green directly, which I have no experience with, and not preswelling from red.. Maybe the idea of visually inspecting the squeegee results before drying might have some value. I have no idea how or why bad squeegeeing (or plate defects for that matter) would cause red blobs on your holos.

posts.post_subject: Please please help me find my processing error!
posts.content_md:
You've got plenty of suggestions on the blobbies but one other thing you may want to consider that will greatly improve the quality and brightness of your holograms is a spatial filter.

[Creative stars](http://www.creativestars.com/catpages/p44.gif) has a good filter for a relatively reasonable price.

You'll be very surprised at the difference one makes when compared to using your average dirty lens.
